did_you_know.text: At the beginning of chapter 33, Elihu addresses Job directly and asks him to listen to what he has to say.
Elihu declares that the Spirit of God made him and that the breath of the Almighty gives him life, presenting himself as a human being dependent on God.
Elihu emphasizes the equality between himself and Job: he too was made from clay, so Job need not be afraid of him.
Elihu summarizes Job’s words as he understands them: Job claimed to be pure, innocent, and free of wrongdoing.
Elihu asks why Job argues with God and reminds him that God is greater than humanity. This shifts the discussion from Job’s complaints to the ways God governs.
According to Elihu, God speaks to people in various ways, but they do not always recognize it.
One of the ways described in the chapter is through a dream or night vision, occurring when a person falls into a deep sleep in bed.
According to Elihu, the purpose of God’s warning is to turn a person away from wrongdoing and save him from pride.
The chapter presents the possibility of an angelic mediator—one who explains to a person the right path he should take.
At the end of his speech, Elihu asks Job to listen in silence, but he still allows Job an opportunity to reply. If Job does not answer, Elihu offers to teach him wisdom.
